strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 3 MLLM families and 5 datasets with consistent improvements over training-free baselines
Clear problem formulation identifying real limitations of Loc-Head and providing intuitive solutions
Strong empirical results achieving comparable or superior performance to training-based methods in several cases (e.g., Qwen2.5VL on Ref-DAVIS: 75.2 vs VISA 69.4)
Thorough ablation studies (Tables 4-7) clearly demonstrating the contribution of each component
Well-executed technical work with sound methodology, good prompt engineering strategy, and reasonable design choices
Practical value as a training-free approach requiring no MLLM modification, with code promised for reproducibility
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty - primarily combines existing techniques (attention rollout, simple subtraction for contrast, averaging for fusion) without introducing fundamentally new concepts
Problematic baseline comparisons: TAM scores are suspiciously low (2.5-3.5) with insufficient investigation; Loc-Head reproduction requires model-specific heuristics making fair comparison difficult

Insufficient justification for key design choices: Why subtraction over other operations for contrastive fusion? Why averaging over learned weighting for complementary fusion? Why the specific attention consistency score formulation?
Does not adequately address fundamental concerns about attention reliability for grounding despite extensive literature on attention being a poor model interpreter
Overstates 'training-free' claim - requires multiple hyperparameter tunings (τ_pq, τ_trk, starting layer) on validation data and extensive prompt engineering
Significant computational overhead not discussed - requires multiple MLLM inference passes (object, background, video-level, frame-level) substantially increasing inference latency
Performance gaps remain substantial: attention-only masks achieve 25.3 J&F (vs 75.2 with SAM), and gaps to SOTA persist on several datasets despite SAM refinement
Failure cases (Fig. 10) reveal important limitations for large sparse objects, thin elongated objects, and briefly appearing small objects, but lack deep investigation into causes
Limited scope of evaluation restricted to VOS tasks; generalization to other grounding tasks and modalities unclear; ReasonVOS only has test set (zero-shot)

strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 5 datasets and 3 MLLM families with thorough ablation studies demonstrating each component's contribution
Strong results on reasoning-intensive tasks (ReasonVOS: 63.9 vs training-based Veason-R1 59.9), demonstrating genuine insight into MLLM reasoning capabilities for localization

Well-motivated training-free approach that works consistently across different MLLM architectures without model-specific modifications, outperforming prior training-free methods (Loc-Head, TAM) by significant margins
Solid technical contributions including vision-aware normalization (V-Max), intuitive contrastive fusion strategy, and attention consistency scoring for filtering false positives

Good reproducibility with code released, consistent prompts across all models/datasets, and detailed implementation details; extensive supplementary analysis including prompt robustness, failure cases, and challenging scenarios
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: individual components represent straightforward applications of existing techniques (attention rollout, simple subtraction for fusion, basic averaging) with empirical rather than principled design choices

Heavy reliance on careful prompt engineering with multiple MLLM inference calls per video, creating unanalyzed computational overhead that may offset training-free benefits; circular dependency where background prompt requires prior object category determination
Marginal or inconsistent improvements over training-based methods: Ref-DAVIS 75.2 vs VRS-HQ 76.0, MeViS 48.1 vs VRS-HQ 50.6; claim of superior performance is overstated given empirical differences

SAM2 dependency undermines training-free claim: coarse attention masks alone achieve poor F-scores (e.g., 15.2 on ReasonVOS), with most improvement coming from SAM2, suggesting localization is primarily SAM2's contribution rather than attention-based insight

Comparison fairness concerns: TAM shows implausibly low performance suggesting task mismatch, Loc-Head required multiple undocumented adaptations (Appendix C), and native Qwen2.5VL grounding baseline (Table 9) relegated to appendix shows smaller gaps than expected

Unaddressed fundamental limitations: large objects with small attention regions cause false filtering (Fig. 9a), small/brief objects missed (Fig. 9c), thin objects undetected (Fig. 9b), and part-level segmentation ambiguity persists despite aligned attention maps

Design choices lack principled justification: penalty term δ in Eq. 8 appears ad-hoc, mean vs Otsu thresholding shows sensitivity (Table 7), starting layer selection varies significantly (Table 5b) without principled selection method, unclear contribution of V-Max normalization to overall improvement

strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 5 datasets and multiple MLLM families with thorough ablation studies
Strong empirical results on reasoning VOS tasks, outperforming all training-based methods on ReasonVOS
Consistent improvements over training-free baselines (Loc-Head, TAM) across different models and datasets
Extensive supplementary analysis including failure cases, prompt robustness studies, and edge case analysis (small objects, multiple objects, part-level, non-explicit expressions)
Good generalization across different MLLM architectures without model-specific modifications
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: core contributions are straightforward combinations of existing techniques (simple subtraction for contrastive fusion, averaging for video-frame fusion, standard SAM2 prompting) with no novel algorithmic or theoretical insights

Weak localization signal from attention maps alone (very low F-scores in Table 1), indicating poor fine-grained spatial understanding and heavy dependence on SAM2 for refinement, making the fusion contribution unclear
Incremental improvements over training-free baselines: 2-5 point gains over Loc-Head, while TAM fails catastrophically (2.5 J&F) making it less meaningful as comparison

Misleading 'training-free' framing: requires multiple carefully designed prompts (three separate MLLM queries per sample) and heavy prompt engineering, contradicting claims of simplicity over training-based approaches

Unfair comparisons with training-based methods: competitive mainly on ReasonVOS only; underperforms on Ref-DAVIS and traditional referring VOS; uses uniform frame sampling while baselines learn keyframe selection; uses different input resolutions for video vs frame-level modalities

Arbitrary design choices lack justification: why simple subtraction for contrastive fusion rather than alternatives, why clamp negatives, why linear combination of s_obj, why average for video-frame fusion rather than learned weighting, why this specific attention consistency score formula
V-Max normalization is a minor modification with modest improvements (72.9→75.2 on Ref-DAVIS) over prior work; unclear why this specific aggregation vs alternatives like entropy-based measures

Fundamental limitations inadequately addressed: Table 7 shows high sensitivity to threshold choices; failure cases (Fig. 9) for large objects, thin structures, small brief objects suggest inherent limitations of attention-based localization without proposed solutions

Limited theoretical justification for why attention rollout should provide localization signals given MLLMs are trained for QA not localization; connection between question-answering attention and object grounding is assumed rather than explained

Missing critical ablations: no ablation on prompt engineering necessity (simpler prompts), no analysis of computational cost vs training-based methods, no quantification of contribution of each prompt vs fusion mechanisms separately

strengths: Well-motivated training-free approach that achieves results competitive with or superior to training-based methods, particularly strong on reasoning VOS (63.9 J&F on ReasonVOS)
Comprehensive experimental validation across 5 datasets, 3 MLLM families, with extensive ablations clearly demonstrating the contribution of each component
Effective technical approach addressing real limitations of attention rollout through intuitive decomposition (contrastive object-background fusion and complementary video-frame fusion)
Strong reproducibility with detailed prompt templates, clear implementation details, and consistency across datasets without model-specific tuning
Thorough analysis including failure cases, prompt robustness studies, and detailed comparison with baseline method limitations in appendix
Practical significance: training-free method demonstrates inherent localization abilities in MLLMs without expensive joint training, improving generalization
weaknesses: Limited novelty in individual components (standard rollout, simple subtraction for contrastive fusion, averaging for video-frame fusion); contribution is primarily in their combination rather than fundamental innovation

Incomplete attribution of improvements—unclear how much performance gain comes from attention fusion vs. the improved SAM2 prompting pipeline, as native Qwen grounding achieves 64.8 vs. 75.2 for DecAF

Prompt engineering complexity not fully acknowledged despite 'training-free' claims—requires three carefully designed prompts (object-focused, background-focused, category choice), adding hidden engineering cost

Fundamental resolution limitation unresolved: attention maps operate at coarse patch resolution; contour accuracy (F) significantly lags region similarity (J), limiting fine-grained boundary localization
Non-trivial failure modes on large objects with sparse attention, small/brief objects, and thin/elongated structures—common scenarios in real videos
Limited theoretical justification for design choices: why subtraction for contrastive fusion? why averaging for video-frame fusion? Mostly empirical rather than principled design
Computational cost not analyzed despite multiple MLLM forward passes and per-frame SAM2 inference; practical scalability unclear
Narrow evaluation scope restricted to VOS tasks; generalization to image grounding or other localization tasks unclear
Method's success directly dependent on MLLM attention quality, but this dependency not thoroughly analyzed; Table 8 shows significant performance degradation with smaller models
